{{Short description|Final of the 2024–25 EFL Cup}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2025}} {{Use British English|date=May 2025}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2025 EFL Cup final | other_titles = | image = Full time at Wembley (geograph 8003233).jpg | caption = [[Wembley Stadium]] at full time | alt = | event = [[2024–25 EFL Cup]] | team1 = [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] | team1score = 1 | team2 = [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] | team2score = 2 | details = | date = {{Start date|2025|3|16|df=y}} | stadium = [[Wembley Stadium]] | city = [[London]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Dan Burn]] ([[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]) | man_of_the_match1atitle = | referee = [[John Brooks (referee)|John Brooks]] ([[Leicestershire and Rutland County Football Association|Leicestershire]]) | attendance = 88,513 | weather = | previous = [[2024 EFL Cup final|2024]] | next = [[2026 EFL Cup final|2026]] }} The '''2025 EFL Cup final''' was the final match of the [[2024–25 EFL Cup]]. It was played between [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] in London, England, on 16 March 2025.{{cite web |last1=Bonn |first1=Kyle |title=When is the 2025 Carabao Cup final? Date, kickoff time of League Cup title match at Wembley Stadium |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/uk/football/news/carabao-cup-final-2025-date-kickoff-time-league-cup/f25d47afa6208d8e3d433659 |website=[[The Sporting News]] |date=5 February 2025}} It was the 65th [[EFL Cup final]] and the 18th to be played at the rebuilt Wembley.{{cite web |first=James M. |last=Ross |title=England - Football League Cup Finals |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engleagcuphist.html |website=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=17 March 2025 |access-date=17 March 2025 |archive-date=17 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317150156/https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engleagcuphist.html |url-status=live }} Newcastle United won the match 2–1 to secure their first EFL Cup title, their first major trophy since the [[1968–69 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] and their first major domestic trophy since the [[1954–55 FA Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62zl58dg8qt|title=Liverpool 1-2 Newcastle: Magpies win Carabao Cup to end 70-year domestic trophy wait|first=Phil|last=McNulty|author-link=Phil McNulty|date=16 March 2025|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=19 March 2025}} ==Route to the final== {{main|2024–25 EFL Cup}} ===Liverpool===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;float:right" |- !scope=col style="width:25px"| Round !scope=col style="width:200px"| Opposition !scope=col style="width:90px"| Score |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| 3 | [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] ([[Anfield|H]]) | 5–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| 4 | [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] ([[Falmer Stadium|A]]) | 3–2 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| QF | [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] ([[St Mary's Stadium|A]]) | 2–1 |- !rowspan="2" scope=row style="text-align:center"| SF | [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] ([[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium|A]]) | 0–1 |- | Tottenham Hotspur ([[Anfield|H]]) | 4–0 |- |colspan="3"| '''Key:''' (H) = Home; (A) = Away |}
As a Premier League club involved in [[UEFA club competitions|UEFA competitions]], Liverpool entered in the third round and were drawn at home to fellow Premier League club [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]. The match was played at [[Anfield]] on 25 September 2024, where Liverpool won 5–1 thanks to goals from [[Diogo Jota]], [[Mohamed Salah]] and [[Cody Gakpo]] and goal for West Ham from an [[own goal]] by [[Jarell Quansah]].{{cite web |last1=Johnston |first1=Neil |title=Liverpool vs West Ham United: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c870dv9gx7zt |work=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the fourth round, they were drawn away to Premier League club [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], played at [[Falmer Stadium]] on 30 October 2024. The match finished with a 3–2 victory for Liverpool, with Gakpo and [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]] both getting on the scoresheet for Liverpool and [[Simon Adingra]] and [[Tariq Lamptey]] scoring for Brighton.{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Gary |title=Gakpo scores twice as holders Liverpool beat Brighton to progress |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5yrr5zdgzpt |work=BBC Sport |date=30 October 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the quarter-finals, Liverpool were drawn away to Premier League club [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], played at [[St Mary's Stadium]] on 18 December 2024. Liverpool recorded a 2–1 victory, with goals coming from [[Darwin Núñez]] and [[Harvey Elliott]] after a Southampton goal from [[Cameron Archer]].{{cite web |last1=Brotherton |first1=Alex |title=Southampton 1–2 Liverpool: Darwin Nunez scores as Reds reach Carabao Cup semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2wjjk2678t |work=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the semi-finals, played over two legs, Liverpool were drawn against Premier League club [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], with the first leg played away at the [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]] on 8 January 2025. Tottenham won the match 1–0 after a late goal by [[Lucas Bergvall]], in a match fuelled with controversy after Liverpool claimed that Bergvall should have been shown a red card for a second yellow card before the goal was scored.{{cite web |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Tottenham 1–0 Liverpool: Lucas Bergvall scores late winner as Spurs beat Liverpool in Carabao Cup semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd608x6l01dt |work=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2025 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} The second leg was played at Anfield on 6 February, where Liverpool produced a dominant display to record a 4–0 victory, with goals coming from Gakpo, Salah, [[Dominik Szoboszlai]] and [[Virgil van Dijk]]. As a result, Liverpool won the tie 4–1 on aggregate to progress to their second consecutive EFL Cup final, and their third in four seasons.{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Jess |title=Liverpool vs Tottenham LIVE |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8y2xv4ygqt |work=BBC Sport |date=6 February 2025 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} ===Newcastle United===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;float:right" |- ! scope="col" style="width:25px" | Round ! scope="col" style="width:200px" | Opposition ! scope="col" style="width:90px" | Score |- ! scope="row" style="text-align:center" |2 | [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] ([[City Ground|A]]) | 1–1 (4–3 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|p.]]) |- ! scope="row" style="text-align:center" |3 | [[AFC Wimbledon]] ([[St James' Park|H]]) | 1–0 |- ! scope="row" style="text-align:center" |4 | [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] ([[St James' Park|H]]) | 2–0 |- ! scope="row" style="text-align:center" |QF | [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] ([[St James' Park|H]]) | 3–1 |- ! rowspan="2" scope="row" style="text-align:center" |SF | [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] ([[Emirates Stadium|A]]) | 2–0 |- | Arsenal ([[St James' Park|H]]) | 2–0 |- | colspan="3" | '''Key:''' (H) = Home; (A) = Away |}
As a Premier League club not involved in any [[UEFA club competitions|UEFA competitions]], Newcastle United entered the cup in the second round where they were drawn away against fellow [[Premier League]] club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]]. The match was played at the [[City Ground]] on 28 August 2024, where Newcastle won 4–3 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] following a 1–1 draw after a goal for Newcastle from [[Joe Willock]] and a goal for Forest from [[Jota Silva]]. [[Callum Hudson-Odoi]], [[Nikola Milenković]] and [[Neco Williams]] all scored their spot kicks for Forest, however, [[Ibrahim Sangaré (Ivorian footballer)|Ibrahim Sangaré]] and [[Taiwo Awoniyi]] missed their penalties for the home side. [[Alexander Isak]], [[Bruno Guimarães]], [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]] and [[Sean Longstaff]] converted their penalties with [[Joelinton]] the only player to miss theirs for the visitors. {{cite news |title=Nottingham Forest vs Newcastle United: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj35z81mmelt |work=BBC Sport |date=28 August 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the third round, they were drawn against [[EFL League Two]] club [[AFC Wimbledon|Wimbledon]], played at [[St James' Park]] on 1 October. The match finished 1–0, with Newcastle's winning goal coming from a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] by defender [[Fabian Schär]] in the first minute of first-half injury time.{{cite news |last1=Abraham |first1=Timothy |title=EFL Cup: Newcastle United v AFC Wimbledon |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9vpme1enrvt |work=BBC Sport |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} The fixture was initially scheduled to be hosted by Wimbledon on 24 September, but was postponed and switched to Newcastle due to flooding at Wimbledon's stadium, [[Plough Lane]].{{cite news |title=Postponed Wimbledon Carabao Cup tie to be played at St James' Park |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cpqz28rgwqlo |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 September 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the fourth round, Newcastle were drawn at home against Premier League club and [[2024 EFL Cup final|2024 finalists]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], with the match played at St James' Park on 30 October. The match saw Newcastle defeat Chelsea 2–0, with goals coming from both Isak and an [[Own goal#Association football|own goal]] from Chelsea defender [[Axel Disasi]].{{cite news |last1=Brotherton |first1=Alex |title=Newcastle United 2–0 Chelsea: Alexander Isak scores as hosts claim impressive win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9dllj2ld85t |work=BBC Sport |date=30 October 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} In the quarter-finals, Newcastle were drawn at home to Premier League club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], with the match played at St James' Park on 18 December. Two goals from [[Sandro Tonali]] inspired Newcastle to a 3–1 victory, with Schär also getting on the scoresheet, as they booked a place in the semi-finals.{{cite news |last1=Sutcliffe |first1=Steve |title=Newcastle United 3–1 Brentford: Newcastle cruise into Carabao Cup semis |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdekddne4edt |work=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2024 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} There, they would face Premier League club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] over two legs, with the first leg played away at the [[Emirates Stadium]] on 7 January 2025. Newcastle beat the Gunners 2–0, with goals from Isak and Gordon giving the Magpies a two-goal advantage in the second leg.{{cite news |last1=Emons |first1=Michael |title=Arsenal vs Newcastle LIVE |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg9dgm5gk4t |work=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2025 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} This was played at St James' Park on 5 February, where Newcastle repeated the first leg scoreline with a 2–0 victory, courtesy of goals from Gordon and [[Jacob Murphy]], as Newcastle won the semi-final 4–0 on aggregate to reach their second final in three seasons.{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Newcastle 2–0 (4–0 agg) Arsenal: Magpies thrash Gunners over two legs to make Carabao Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1we9vxz7xdt |work=BBC Sport |date=5 February 2025 |access-date=6 February 2025 }} ==Pre-match== === Background === This was Newcastle's third appearance in the final, having previously lost in 1976 and 2023. Liverpool were the reigning EFL Cup holders and were appearing in a record fifteenth final, having won the cup a record 10 times. Newcastle were aiming to end one of the longest trophy droughts in English football,{{Cite web |title=Last Major Trophy Won by English Clubs from 1874-2022 |url=https://www.myfootballfacts.com/england_footy/english-domestic/last-major-trophy-won-by-english-clubs/ |access-date=23 February 2023 |website=My Football Facts}} with their last major honour being the [[1968–69 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]]. Their most recent major domestic trophy was even earlier, when they won the [[1954–55 FA Cup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.football365.com/news/the-big-sixs-longest-trophy-droughts-and-how-they-ended|title=Big Six longest trophy droughts and how they eventually ended as Spurs edge towards 15 years|work=Football365.com|first=Ian|last=Watson|date=10 October 2022}} === Team news === [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]] missed the final for Newcastle after receiving a red card in an [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]] defeat against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton and Hove Albion]] for a challenge on [[Jan Paul van Hecke]] on 2 March.{{cite news |title=Anthony Gordon: Newcastle winger to miss Carabao Cup final with Lewis Hall out for season through injury |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13321132/anthony-gordon-newcastle-winger-to-miss-carabao-cup-final-after-club-decide-not-to-appeal-red-card-against-brighton |work=Sky Sports |date=5 March 2025 |access-date=5 March 2025 }} [[Lewis Hall (footballer)|Lewis Hall]] and [[Sven Botman]] would also miss the final with Hall out for the remainder of the season with a foot injury and Botman ruled out for eight weeks with another knee injury.{{Cite web |title=Hall to miss rest of the season with foot injury |publisher=Newcastle United |url=https://www.newcastleunited.com/en/news/hall-to-miss-rest-of-the-season-with-foot-injury |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=newcastleunited.com }}{{Cite web |date=2025-03-07 |title=Newcastle United defender Sven Botman ruled out for eight weeks with knee injury |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5y0py775kxo |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=BBC Sport }} Five of Newcastle's starting line-up had started the 2023 final, while two had appeared off the bench. Callum Wilson, who appeared off the bench, had started the 2023 final and Joe Willock played as a substitute on both occasions. For Liverpool, [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]], [[Conor Bradley]], [[Joe Gomez]], and [[Tyler Morton]] all missed the final due to injury.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-14 |title=Injured Alexander-Arnold out of League Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c778ex3278zo |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=BBC Sport }} Newcastle were the first side to win the cup with as many as six English starters in the final since [[Leicester City]] in the [[1997 Football League Cup final]]. Runners-up [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] were the last team to field that many English starters in a final, in the [[2013 Football League Cup final]]. ==Match== === Summary === In the final minute of the first half, [[Dan Burn]] scored with a header to the left corner of the net after a corner from the left from [[Kieran Trippier]] to give Newcastle a 1–0 lead at half-time.{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/mar/16/newcastle-sink-liverpool-to-savour-taste-of-glory-after-decades-of-drought|title=Newcastle sink Liverpool to savour taste of glory after decades of drought|date=16 March 2025|work=Guardian|accessdate=19 March 2025}} In the 52nd minute, [[Alexander Isak]] scored with a half-volley low to the left of the net to give Newcastle a 2–0 lead. {{external media | float = right | width = 300px | video1 = [https://x.com/NUFC/status/1903018243859603955 Second goal of the match.]{{Cite tweet |user=NUFC |number=1903018243859603955 |title=Limbs}}}} In the fourth minute of time added on Liverpool substitute [[Federico Chiesa]] scored with a low left footed finish to make it 2–1.
